content:
It might not be the wrong password, but it might be wrong for the server settings or username.

It would be helpful if you could provide a bit more information.

What OS are you using ? Windows. MAC, Linux ? What version of Thunderbird are you using? Did you get Thunderbird from official website https://www.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/all/ or via Windows App Store or flatpak or snap etc ?

What server are you using eg: gmail, AOL, BT etc ? It's useful to know what server you are using because some require you to use an app specific password and some require you to select to allow third party access.

What Anti-Virus are you using?

Are you setting up an Imap or Pop mail account ?

To ensure nothing is blocking Thunderbird do the following anyway as it needs setting up.

Firewall: Firewall may be controlled by the default provided by OS OR it might be controlled by an Anti-Virus you installed. Access Firewall and set up Thunderbird as an allowed program.

VPN: Please check your computer to see there is a VPN operating. Some Anti-virus products provide VPN and it might be running by default. Many server do not VPN as it hides your IP address. eg: Gmail does not like VPN. Please switch off the VPN.

This problem does not appear only on the latest version of Thunderbird. When I had it on version 115.10.1 (64 bit). When I updated to the latest version of Thunderbird (153.1 Oesr (64 bit)) the problem persisted. So far as I have seen on these posts everyone that has had this problem had email addresses tied to "charter.net". I have not seen anyone using any other mail server. I have to wonder about people whose email address ends in "spectrum.net" or "spectrum.com", because Spectrum bought out Charter some years ago.

Many years ago I found out that the code being used for the email server owned by Charter was using code from a company (I have long since forgotten it's name) that had gone out of business and had failed to code their server code to support an IEEE standard specifying how to support sub-folders that contain blanks in their name. (I see now a statement that IEEE no longer specifies standards for emails, that is now IEFT that provides standards for email. I am not sure I trust this statement.) Sub-folders is a technique I have almost for ever used to organize emails that i have received, i.e. in subject categories. I used to use blanks in the sub-folder names, but when I moved to Charter.net (during a physical move from one state to another). I had to quit putting blanks in sub-folder names. The code on Charter.net servers did not comply with the IEEE standard on how blanks in folder names was to be handled across the internet, while Thunderbird complied with said standard. I had collected IEEE standard file names then but have since lost that file.
